title: Dust and infection control during building work near patients
audience: Cleaners and post-construction clean crews working in or beside healthcare buildings, including dental and aged care sites.
learningOutcomes: Explain why building dust is an infection hazard in patient areas.
Identify the boundary between the construction clean and the hospital clean.
Check barriers and dust controls before starting cleaning near active works.

instruction.heading: Why building work is an infection issue
instruction.body: Demolition, drilling, sanding, and the stripping of ceilings and floor coverings release dust into the air and onto surfaces. People with weakened defences, and areas such as operating rooms, dialysis units and bone marrow units, are harmed by that dust. The source therefore treats building work as an infection control task with its own risk assessment, not as ordinary maintenance.

instruction.heading: Two kinds of clean
instruction.body: The construction team cleans the works zone after the day's labour stops, or more often when needed, to remove heavy soil, dust, debris and building material. The hospital clean begins outside the hoarding, where the works zone stops, and is done by facility staff. Know where that boundary sits before you start, because each team has different tasks and each has to deal with dust left on its side.

instruction.heading: Matching the work to the risk
instruction.body: Before work starts, the infection prevention team looks at three things. The first is the kind of building activity, graded from A, a visual check with little dust, to D, major demolition or new construction across several shifts. The second is the patient area affected, graded from low risk, for example offices, to highest risk, including intensive care, operating rooms, isolation rooms and units caring for people with weakened immunity. The third is the precautions class, which the source reads from a matrix that combines the first two. The matrix is not reproduced here. Learners use the matrix their own infection prevention team has approved.

instruction.heading: Precautions you may see on site
instruction.body: Higher precaution classes call for dust containment, sealed barriers between the works zone and the remainder of the building, changes to air handling, sealed waste containers, dust mats at entrances, HEPA-filtered vacuums in clinical areas, wet cleaning in place of sweeping, and no taking down of barriers until the infection prevention team has inspected the job. Check that barriers are intact before each shift begins, and report any gap immediately.

procedure: Ask the IPC team to confirm the activity type and the precautions class for the area before any cleaning task begins.
Check that the barriers and dust mats are intact and sealed before you enter the area.
Keep brooms out of clinical areas, and use the vacuum type the plan names.
Wet clean or wipe down work surfaces using detergent in water, and disinfect in clinical areas where the plan requires it.
Keep construction waste in covered containers until it leaves the site.
Never take a barrier away until the IPC team has inspected and cleared the job.
Record the inspection, the barrier check and any gap you found.

workedExamples.situation: A ward bathroom refurbishment involves sanding plaster on a wall beside an occupied bed space. The area is a medium-risk unit.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner check before the shift starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: Ask the IPC team to confirm the activity type and the precautions class. Check the barriers and the dust mat, and confirm that the vacuum in use is the type the plan names. Report any gap before cleaning begins.

workedExamples.situation: A contractor asks you to take down a barrier at 4 pm so that a delivery can pass.
workedExamples.reasoning: Leave the barrier where it is. Only the IPC team clears barrier removal, after inspection. Report the request to your supervisor and the IPC team.

equipmentAndPpe: Disposable gloves and protective clothing matched to the task
HEPA-filtered vacuum where the plan requires one
Dust mats at entrances and exits to the work area
Detergent, water and the approved disinfectant for clinical areas

commonErrors.prevention: Use the wet method or the vacuum that the plan names.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the construction crew has finished cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm where the works zone ends and what the hospital clean covers.

commonErrors.error: Removing a barrier to get the job done faster.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep barriers in place until the IPC team clears the work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Dust from building work near patients can carry organisms. Treat dust in a clinical area as a possible infection hazard.
This lesson covers cleaning beside building work. It does not cover construction licensing or induction, which the work owner must arrange.
The four activity types and the class matrix are the source's approach. An Australian site must use its own infection prevention team's approved method.
Construction waste goes into covered containers, then follows the site's waste plan under “Clinical waste: segregation, containers and handling”.

qualityStandard: Barriers are checked and recorded before every shift.
No barrier is removed before the infection prevention team has cleared the work.
documentationEvidence: Activity type and precautions class recorded from the IPC team's plan
Barrier check log with time and initials
IPC clearance recorded before barrier removal
summary: Building dust is an infection hazard in patient areas, so it is handled as a risk task.
The construction clean ends at the hoarding, and the hospital clean begins outside it.
Check barriers and dust controls before work, and never take a barrier down before clearance.

knowledgeChecks.question: Who usually carries out the construction clean of a works zone after the day's labour stops?
options: The construction team, to remove heavy soil, dust and debris inside the works zone.
Patients in the next room and the visitors who are waiting in the corridor
The infection prevention team alone without the works crew on site today
Nobody, because the hospital clean covers it and the contractor signs it off early

knowledgeChecks.question: How is the precautions class for building work chosen?
options: From the activity type and the patient area affected, using the IPC team's matrix.
By the contractor's preference and the price the contractor is paid for the job
By the weekday shift that the crew is rostered on and the number of workers on the job
By choosing the option with the most ward space available for the crew

knowledgeChecks.question: When may a barrier come down once building work finishes?
options: The moment the workers leave the site and the dust has settled overnight
When the IPC team has inspected the job and cleared the removal.
When the cleaner judges the area tidy and the rubbish has been bagged up
The moment the contractor asks for it and the shift has ended
